The 20/40 rule may be met with glasses or contacts.
The applicant meets the normal standard, so no daylight-only limit is needed.

questions.q: Which statement about applicants with monocular vision (blind in one eye) is correct?
options: They need 20/20 in the other eye to drive
They cannot get certain special licenses or endorsements
They may never hold any kind of Connecticut driver's license
They may drive only with a licensed parent in the car until age 21
questions.ref: p.5 The Vision Test: persons with monocular vision do not qualify for certain special licenses or endorsements (the other eye must be 20/40 with a 100-degree field).
questions.why: People with vision in only one eye do not qualify for certain special licenses or endorsements. (Driver's Manual, page 5)
wrong: The other eye needs at least 20/40, not 20/20, with a field of 100 degrees or more.
They can get a license if the other eye meets 20/40 and the field of vision rule.
The manual has no such rule for people with one-eye vision.

questions.q: Your side vision lets you notice a car on your right while looking ahead. Why does the manual say you must still use your side mirrors or glance to the side?
options: Because side vision fades at highway speeds
Because you cannot focus on things off to the side
Because mirrors show traffic in front of you
Because the law forbids relying on side vision alone while driving
questions.ref: p.5 Side Vision: because you cannot focus on things to the side, you must also use your side mirrors or glance to the side if necessary.
questions.why: Side vision lets you notice things, but you cannot focus on things off to the side. So you must also use your side mirrors or glance to the side. (Driver's Manual, page 5)
wrong: The manual's reason is that you cannot focus to the side, not anything about speed.
Side mirrors show the sides of your car, not what is in front of you.
The manual's reason is that you cannot focus on things to the side, not a law.

questions.q: According to the manual, judging distances and speeds well is especially important in which situation?
options: Judging safe openings when passing on two-lane roads
Reading the speed limit signs posted along the interstate highway
Spotting the dashboard warning lights early
Adjusting the mirrors before the road test
questions.ref: p.5 Judging Distances and Speeds: especially important in knowing how far you are from other vehicles and judging safe openings when merging and passing on two-lane roads.
questions.why: Judging distances and speeds is especially important for knowing how far you are from other vehicles, and for judging safe gaps when merging and passing on two-lane roads. (Driver's Manual, page 5)
wrong: Reading signs is about clear vision, not judging distances and speeds.
Seeing warning lights is not what the manual links to judging distances and speeds.
Adjusting mirrors is not what the manual links to judging distances and speeds.

questions.q: A driver who sees well in daylight notices trouble with the glare of oncoming headlights after dark. What does the manual advise?
options: Wear sunglasses at night to cut down on headlight glare
Night driving is fine as long as you passed the vision test at the DMV
Use high beams so that oncoming drivers will dim their own headlights
Don't drive more than necessary at night, and be very careful
questions.ref: p.5 Night Vision: if you have problems seeing at night, don't drive more than is necessary and be very careful when you do.
questions.why: If you have trouble seeing at night, don't drive more than you need to, and be very careful when you do. (Driver's Manual, page 5)
wrong: The manual's advice is to limit night driving and be very careful, not to wear sunglasses.
Many people who see well in daylight still have trouble at night, so passing the vision test is not enough.
Do not try to get back at drivers with your high beams, or you may both be blinded.

questions.q: How often does the manual say you should have your eyes checked by an eye specialist?
options: Every year or two
Only when you renew
Every three months
Every five years
questions.ref: p.5 The Vision Test: you should have your eyes checked every year or two by an eye specialist.
questions.why: Have your eyes checked every year or two by an eye specialist. (Driver's Manual, page 5)
wrong: The manual says every year or two, not just at renewal.
The manual says every year or two, not every three months.
The manual says every year or two, not every five years.

questions.q: Which statement about drivers with hearing problems is TRUE according to the manual?
options: Their driving records are much worse, so they need a limited license
They must have a passenger with good hearing ride along whenever they drive
Their driving records are just as good as drivers with good hearing
They may not drive on highways because they cannot hear sirens
questions.ref: p.5 The Vision Test (hearing): studies have shown that the driving records of hearing-impaired drivers are just as good as those of drivers with good hearing.
questions.why: Studies show hearing-impaired drivers have driving records just as good as drivers with good hearing. (Driver's Manual, page 5)
wrong: Their records are just as good, so this is false.
The manual has no such rule. These drivers learn to rely more on their vision.
The manual has no such rule. These drivers adjust and stay more alert.

questions.q: Which statement about hearing and driving is FALSE according to the manual?
options: Hearing loss always comes on suddenly, so drivers notice it right away
The sound of horns, a siren, or screeching tires can warn a driver of danger
Hearing problems, like bad eyesight, can come on very slowly
Deaf drivers learn to rely more on their vision and tend to stay more alert
questions.ref: p.5 Hearing: hearing problems, like bad eyesight, can come on so slowly that you do not notice them; deaf drivers rely more on vision and stay alert.
questions.why: This is false. Hearing problems, like bad eyesight, can come on so slowly that you do not notice them. (Driver's Manual, page 5)
wrong: This is true. The manual says horns, sirens, and screeching tires can warn you of danger.
This is true. The manual says hearing problems can come on very slowly.
This is true. The manual says deaf drivers rely more on vision and stay more alert.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the ways a 16- or 17-year-old may complete the required driver training program?
options: Home training plus the 8-hour course
Studying this manual alone with no course
A licensed commercial driving school
A secondary school (high school) program
questions.ref: p.6 16- and 17-Year-Old Applicants: training must be through a licensed commercial driving school, a secondary school program, or home training plus the eight-hour safe driving course.
questions.why: Teens must finish a training program through a commercial driving school, a high school program, or home training plus the 8-hour course. Reading the manual alone does not count. (Driver's Manual, page 6)
wrong: Home training plus the 8-hour safe driving course is one of the allowed ways.
A licensed commercial driving school is one of the allowed ways.
A secondary school program is one of the allowed ways.

questions.q: A DMV-approved commercial or secondary school driver education program for teens consists of how many hours of classroom instruction?
options: 20 hours
30 hours
8 hours
40 hours
questions.ref: p.6 Commercial Driving School or Secondary School Training: 30 hours of classroom instruction and at least 40 hours of behind-the-wheel training.
questions.why: A DMV-approved school program has 30 hours of classroom instruction and at least 40 hours behind the wheel. (Driver's Manual, page 6)
wrong: The classroom part is 30 hours, not 20.
Eight hours is the safe driving practices course, not the full classroom part.
Forty hours is the behind-the-wheel training, not the classroom part.

questions.q: A teen finishes a commercial driving school course. What document does the school issue that the teen needs to be eligible for the road test?
options: A signed home instructor statement
A temporary paper driver's license
A Medical Review Division clearance letter from DMV
A course completion certificate (form CS-1)
questions.ref: p.6 Commercial Driving School or Secondary School Training: the school will issue a course completion certificate (form CS-1), required to be eligible for the road test.
questions.why: After the course, the school issues a course completion certificate, form CS-1. You need it to be eligible for the road test. (Driver's Manual, page 6)
wrong: The signed home instructor statement is for home-trained applicants, not school students.
A temporary paper license is given only after you pass the road test.
A medical clearance letter is needed only if DMV requires a medical review.

questions.q: A 16-year-old is home trained by a parent for all 40 hours of driving and takes only the 8-hour safe driving course at a driving school. How long after the permit is issued must she wait to take the road test?
options: 180 days
90 days
120 days
60 days
questions.ref: p.6 Commercial/Secondary and Home Training: applicants without full school driver education (or full 30 hours classroom plus 8 hours school behind-the-wheel) must wait 180 days after the permit is issued.
questions.why: Applicants who do not finish full driver education at a school must wait 180 days after the permit is issued. Home training with only the 8-hour course falls in this group. (Driver's Manual, page 6)
wrong: Ninety days is the wait for applicants 18 or older.
The 120-day wait is only for those who finish a full school program.
The manual has no 60-day wait. This applicant must wait 180 days.

questions.q: When must a home instructor sign the statement that the applicant got a permit and completed at least 30 hours of course study?
options: When the license card is mailed
When the permit is first issued
Before the knowledge test
At the time of the road test
questions.ref: p.6 Home Training Program: the home instructor must sign a statement at the time of the road test.
questions.why: The home instructor must sign the statement at the time of the road test. (Driver's Manual, page 6)
wrong: The statement is signed at the road test, before any license is mailed.
The statement confirms training that happens after the permit, so it is signed at the road test.
The statement is signed at the road test, not before the knowledge test.

questions.q: What must a home training course cover?
options: Only the material that will be scored on the road test checklist
Only the teen driving laws covered in the parent training
All the material in this manual, plus other needed information
Only the road signs and pavement markings chapter of the manual
questions.ref: p.6 Home Training Program: the home training course must cover all of the material in this manual and other necessary driver education information.
questions.why: A home training course must cover all of the material in this manual, plus other information needed to drive safely. (Driver's Manual, page 6)
wrong: It must cover all of the manual, not just road test items.
It must cover all of the manual, not just teen laws.
It must cover all of the manual, not just one chapter.

questions.q: A home-trained teen must show a course completion certificate for the approved eight-hour course. Which form is it?
options: Form B-230
Form CS-1 a
Form CS-1
Form R-1
questions.ref: p.6 Home Training Program: home-trained applicants must show a course completion certificate (form CS-1 a) from a secondary or commercial driving school.
questions.why: Home-trained teens must show form CS-1 a, a course completion certificate for the approved eight-hour course. (Driver's Manual, page 6)
wrong: The manual names form CS-1 a, not B-230.
Form CS-1 is the certificate from a full school program. Home-trained teens show CS-1 a.
The manual names form CS-1 a, not R-1.

questions.q: Which statement about the eight-hour safe driving course required of home-trained teens is FALSE?
options: It includes the two-hour mandatory parent training class
It includes at least four hours on alcohol and drugs
It may be taken from the DMV-approved home instructor
It is also required of 16- and 17-year-olds licensed out of state
questions.ref: p.6 Home Training Program: the CS-1 a must come from a local secondary school or commercial driving school; the course includes 4 hours on alcohol/drugs and the 2-hour parent class; also required of out-of-state 16-17 year-old licensed drivers.
questions.why: This is false. The eight-hour course must come from a local secondary school or a commercial driving school, not the home instructor. (Driver's Manual, page 6)
wrong: This is true. The course includes the two-hour parent training class.
This is true. The course has at least four hours on alcohol and drugs.
This is true. Out-of-state licensed 16- and 17-year-olds also need it.

questions.q: A 16-year-old completes 25 hours of behind-the-wheel training at a driving school and 15 hours with a qualified parent. Does this meet the 40-hour behind-the-wheel requirement?
options: Yes, any mix of school and home training may be used
No, all 40 hours must be at a driving school
Yes, but only if the parent is a licensed instructor
No, at least 30 hours must be home training
questions.ref: p.7: all 16- and 17-year-old applicants must have at least 40 hours of behind-the-wheel training, which may be any combination of professional (driving school) or home training.
questions.why: Teens need at least 40 hours behind the wheel. Any mix of driving school and home training can be used. (Driver's Manual, page 7)
wrong: The hours do not all have to be at a school. Any mix counts.
The parent does not need to be a licensed instructor, just a qualified home trainer.
The manual allows any mix, with no minimum for home training.

questions.q: Kai is 18 and just got a learner's permit. He wants to practice with his 19-year-old cousin, who has been licensed for three years. Is this allowed?
options: No, an 18-year-old must use a driving school only
Yes, if the cousin's license was never suspended
No, a qualified trainer must be at least 20 years old
Yes, trainer rules no longer apply at age 18
questions.ref: p.7 Applicants 18 Years of Age or Older: the permit holder must be accompanied by a school instructor or a qualified trainer age 20 or older with a license unsuspended for four or more consecutive years.
questions.why: A qualified trainer must be at least 20 years old and licensed for four or more years with no suspension. A 19-year-old cousin does not qualify. (Driver's Manual, page 7)
wrong: An adult permit holder may also use a qualified trainer, not only a school.
The cousin is too young and has not been licensed for four years.
Trainer rules still apply to permit holders 18 and older.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed in the manual as something you should know before you take your road test?
options: When to stop for a yellow signal
How to change a flat tire
How to park properly on a hill
How to control the car in reverse
questions.ref: p.7 Things you should know before you take your test: speed, turning, right of way, stopping for a yellow signal, backing, and parking (including on a hill).
questions.why: The list covers speed, turning, right of way, stopping for yellow lights, backing, and parking. Changing a flat tire is not on it. (Driver's Manual, page 7)
wrong: Knowing when to stop for a yellow signal is on the list.
Parking the right way on a hill is on the list.
Controlling your car in reverse is on the list.

questions.q: You arrive for your road test and are walking to the test vehicle. What does the manual say you should do before getting in?
options: Ask the examiner which route you will take
Look for nearby parked cars, people, or objects
Check the engine oil level and the pressure in each tire
Honk the horn to alert people nearby
questions.ref: p.7 Things you should remember during your test: prior to entering the test vehicle, observe nearby parked cars, people, or objects that could affect your ability to safely put the car in motion.
questions.why: Before getting in, look for nearby parked cars, people, or objects that could affect pulling away safely. (Driver's Manual, page 7)
wrong: The manual says to follow the directions you are given, not to ask about the route.
The manual's tip before getting in is to look around the car, not to check oil and tires.
The horn is only for warning others, so do not honk for no reason.

questions.q: During your road test, the car is in "park" and you are ready to pull out. What should you do before shifting into gear?
options: Release the parking brake
Sound the horn once
Turn on the hazard lights
Apply the brake
questions.ref: p.7 Things you should remember during your test: apply the brake before you shift the car into gear from the "park" position.
questions.why: Apply the brake before you shift the car out of park and into gear. (Driver's Manual, page 7)
wrong: The manual's tip is to put your foot on the brake first.
The horn is only for warning others, not for pulling out.
Hazard lights are for car trouble, not for starting to drive.

questions.q: The examiner asks you to show how you would signal a turn if your turn signals did not work. What does the manual say you should be able to do?
options: Use your four-way hazard lights
Tap your horn twice at the turn
Flash your headlights at traffic
Demonstrate hand signals
questions.ref: p.7 Things you should remember during your test: use the turn signals every time it is appropriate and be able to demonstrate hand signals.
questions.why: You should use your turn signals every time it is right to, and be able to show hand signals. (Driver's Manual, page 7)
wrong: Hazard lights show that your car is having trouble, not which way you are turning.
A horn does not show a turn. The manual says to know hand signals.
Flashing headlights does not show a turn. The manual says to know hand signals.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT required for the vehicle you bring to your road test?
options: It must be registered in the applicant's own name
It must be mechanically safe to operate
It must suit the license class applied for
It must have valid proof of insurance with it on test day
questions.ref: p.7 The Road Test: you must appear with a vehicle appropriate for the license class, mechanically safe, with valid registration and proof of insurance (a properly insured long-term leased vehicle may be used).
questions.why: The test car must suit the license class, be safe, and have valid registration and insurance. It does not have to be in your own name. (Driver's Manual, page 7)
wrong: The car must be mechanically safe, or the test will not be given.
The car must suit the license class you are applying for.
The car must have proof of insurance.

questions.q: A new driver passes the road test. How much must be paid for the license?
questions.ref: p.7 To Begin the Road Test You Will Need: License Fees - you must pay $84 for a license after you pass the road test.
questions.why: You must pay 84 dollars for a license after you pass the road test. (Driver's Manual, page 7)
wrong: The license fee is 84 dollars, not 40.
Thirty dollars is the duplicate license fee, not the license fee.
The license fee is 84 dollars, not 72.

questions.q: An applicant had a medical condition reviewed before getting a permit. What extra item may this applicant need to begin the road test?
options: A note from the applicant's school nurse
A letter from the applicant's auto insurance agent saying it is covered
A second vision test from an eye doctor
A clearance letter from the DMV Medical Review Division
questions.ref: p.7 To Begin the Road Test You Will Need: a clearance letter from DMV Medical Review Division (only if required, see First Time Drivers).
questions.why: If DMV required a medical review, you need a clearance letter from the DMV Medical Review Division to begin the road test. (Driver's Manual, page 7)
wrong: The manual names a DMV clearance letter, not a school nurse note.
Proof of insurance is for the car, not a medical clearance.
The manual names a DMV clearance letter, not a second vision test.

questions.q: Which item is NOT on the list of things every applicant needs to begin the road test?
options: A diploma from high school
Proof of the 8-hour course
Your current learner's permit
The license fee
questions.ref: p.7 To Begin the Road Test You Will Need: your learner's permit, proof of the 8-hour safe driving course (CS-1), license fees, and a medical clearance letter only if required.
questions.why: To begin the road test you need your permit, proof of the 8-hour course, and the license fee. A high school diploma is not on the list. (Driver's Manual, page 7)
wrong: Proof of the 8-hour safe driving course, form CS-1, is on the list.
Your learner's permit is on the list.
The license fee is on the list.

questions.q: During your road test, the examiner asks you to turn on the defroster and then the windshield washers. Why?
options: Operating vehicle equipment is part of the road test
The examiner is checking it for an emissions test
It shows the car passed its safety inspection
It is only done if the test is held in the winter
questions.ref: p.8 The road test evaluates: operation of vehicle equipment such as wipers and washers, heater and defroster, parking brake, headlights and high beams, and the horn.
questions.why: The road test checks how you use vehicle equipment, like wipers and washers, the heater and defroster, lights, and the horn. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: The road test is not an emissions test. It checks that you can use the equipment.
The road test checks your skills, not the car's inspection.
Using equipment is part of every road test, not just in winter.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed among the things the road test evaluates?
options: Adjusting the seat and the mirrors
Recognizing warning lights on the panel
Responding to emergency vehicles
Checking the engine oil level
questions.ref: p.8 The road test evaluates: adjusting seat, mirrors, steering wheel and seat belts; operating equipment; response to signs, signals and emergency vehicles; backing/parking; turns; recognizing instrument-panel warning lights; other maneuvers.
questions.why: The road test checks seat and mirror setup, equipment use, response to signs and emergency vehicles, and warning lights. Checking oil is not listed. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: Adjusting the seat and mirrors is listed.
Recognizing warning lights on the panel is listed.
Responding to emergency vehicles is listed.

questions.q: You are paying your license fee by check at a DMV branch office. To whom should the check be made payable?
options: Your town clerk
The driving school
DMV
The State Treasurer
questions.ref: p.8 Pay for Your License: please make all checks payable to DMV.
questions.why: Make all checks payable to DMV. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: Checks go to DMV, not your town clerk.
Checks go to DMV, not the driving school.
Checks go to DMV, not the State Treasurer.

questions.q: Two months after getting his license, a 16-year-old wants to drive his mother and father to dinner. Only his mother holds a valid license. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, but only after his first six months
No, both of his parents must hold valid driver's licenses
No, he may not drive his parents together
Yes, if at least one parent holds a valid license
questions.ref: p.8 Passenger Restrictions: during the first six months, passengers may include his or her parents or legal guardian, at least one of whom holds a valid driver's license.
questions.why: In the first six months, a new teen driver may carry his parents, as long as at least one of them holds a valid license. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: Parents are allowed even in the first six months.
Only one parent needs a valid license.
Parents may ride together if at least one has a valid license.

questions.q: Four months after getting her license, a 17-year-old wants to drive two neighbors, both 30 years old and licensed for ten years with no suspensions. Is this allowed?
options: No, only one such qualified adult may ride
Yes, as long as each has a seat belt
Yes, both are over 20 and qualified
No, only a licensed instructor may ride
questions.ref: p.8 Passenger Restrictions: during the first six months, the exception is one person at least 20 years old who has held a license for four or more consecutive years without suspension.
questions.why: In the first six months, the exception is for one person who is at least 20 and licensed for four years with no suspension. Two neighbors is too many. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: Seat belts are a separate rule. Only one qualified adult may ride.
Both qualify, but the rule allows only one such person.
A licensed instructor is one option, but so are parents or one qualified adult.

questions.q: A 17-year-old licensed driver leaves home at 5:15 a.m. to go to the gym. Does this violate the curfew?
options: Yes, the curfew lasts until 5:30 a.m.
No, the curfew ends at 5 a.m.
Yes, the curfew ends at 6 a.m.
Yes, gym trips are never allowed
questions.ref: p.8 Hour Restrictions (Curfew): 11 p.m. to 5 a.m.
questions.why: The teen curfew runs from 11 at night to 5 in the morning. At 5:15 in the morning, it is over. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: The curfew ends at 5 in the morning, not 5:30.
The curfew ends at 5 in the morning, not 6.
The curfew ends at 5 in the morning, so a gym trip after that is fine.

questions.q: At midnight, a 17-year-old who is an active volunteer ambulance service member drives a friend home from a party. Do the curfew and passenger restrictions apply?
options: Yes, the exemption covers only emergency calls and active duties
No, active volunteer ambulance members are exempt from them at all times
No, as long as the ambulance service gave permission
Yes, but only the curfew applies to him, not the passenger restriction
questions.ref: p.8 Please note: the restrictions do not apply to active volunteer fire, ambulance or EMS members responding to or returning from an emergency call or carrying out duties as an active member.
questions.why: The exemption covers only going to or coming back from an emergency call, or doing duties as an active member. Driving a friend from a party is not covered. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: The exemption is not for all times. It covers only emergency calls and duties.
Permission from the service is not part of the exemption.
Both the curfew and the passenger rules apply when the teen is not on emergency duty.

questions.q: A 17-year-old just got a motorcycle endorsement. For how long may he NOT carry a passenger on a motorcycle?
options: Until his 18th birthday, regardless of the date issued
Three months after the endorsement is issued
Six months after the endorsement is issued
One full year after the endorsement is issued
questions.ref: p.8 Other Restrictions: 16- and 17-year-old drivers may not transport any passenger on a motorcycle for six months after the issuance of a motorcycle endorsement.
questions.why: Teen drivers may not carry any passenger on a motorcycle for six months after the endorsement is issued. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: The rule is six months from the endorsement, not until age 18.
The rule is six months, not three.
The rule is six months, not one year.

questions.q: Ten months after getting his license, a 17-year-old wants to drive his parents and four siblings in a car with five seat belts. Is this allowed?
options: No, he may carry only one sibling at a time
No, he may not carry more passengers than seat belts
Yes, because all of the passengers are members of his immediate family
Yes, since his parents are riding with him
questions.ref: p.8 Passenger Restrictions and Other Restrictions: family is allowed after six months, but 16- and 17-year-olds may not transport more passengers than the number of seatbelts (seven people, five belts).
questions.why: Teen drivers may not carry more passengers than there are seat belts. Six passengers in a car with five belts breaks this rule. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: After six months, immediate family members are allowed, so siblings are fine.
Family is allowed after six months, but not more passengers than seat belts.
Having parents in the car does not change the seat belt rule.

questions.q: A 17-year-old licensed driver is offered a summer job driving a vanpool vehicle. What does the manual say?
options: It is allowed once the teen is licensed six months
16- and 17-year-olds may not operate a vanpool vehicle
It is allowed if no passenger is under age 18
It is allowed only during daylight hours
questions.ref: p.8 Other Restrictions: 16- and 17-year-old licensed drivers may not operate any vehicle that requires a public passenger transportation permit or a vanpool vehicle.
questions.why: 16- and 17-year-old drivers may not operate a vanpool vehicle. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: The vanpool ban applies to all 16- and 17-year-olds, not just new drivers.
Passenger ages do not matter. Teens may not drive a vanpool at all.
Daylight does not matter. Teens may not drive a vanpool at all.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a way the manual lists to register as an organ and tissue donor?
options: By calling your local hospital
By mail on the Change of Address form
When you obtain or renew a license
Online at the DMV website
questions.ref: p.8 Becoming an Organ and Tissue Donor: register when you obtain or renew a license or ID card, online at ct.gov/dmv, or by mail with DMV's Change of Address form.
questions.why: You can register as a donor when you get or renew a license, online at the DMV website, or by mail on the Change of Address form. Calling a hospital is not listed. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: Registering by mail on the Change of Address form is listed.
Registering when you get or renew a license is listed.
Registering online at the DMV website is listed.

questions.q: How much does it cost to be registered as an organ and tissue donor when you get your driver's license?
options: A $10 fee
A $30 fee
Nothing
An $84 fee
questions.ref: p.8 Becoming an Organ and Tissue Donor: there is "no fee" to be registered as an organ and tissue donor.
questions.why: There is no fee to be registered as an organ and tissue donor. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: The manual says there is no fee.
Thirty dollars is the fee for a duplicate license, not for signing up.
Eighty-four dollars is the license fee, not a donor fee.

questions.q: You already have a valid license and want to add the organ donor insignia to it now. What must you do?
options: Order a duplicate credential and pay a $30 fee
Nothing; it is added free at your next renewal visit
Mail a letter to your town hall asking for a sticker
Retake the vision test and pay the $84 license fee
questions.ref: p.8 Becoming an Organ and Tissue Donor: to add or remove the insignia on a valid license or ID, you need to order a duplicate credential and pay a $30.00 duplicate credential fee.
questions.why: To add the donor mark to a license you already have, order a duplicate credential and pay a 30 dollar fee. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: The manual says you must order a duplicate and pay the fee to add it now.
The manual does not mention a sticker from your town hall.
You do not retake any test. You order a duplicate for 30 dollars.

questions.q: For which people is being included in the Organ and Tissue Donor Registry legal authorization for donation?
options: Individuals 21 and over
Individuals 16 and over
Any age, with no limit
Individuals 18 and over
questions.ref: p.8 Becoming an Organ and Tissue Donor: for individuals 18 and over, being included in the Registry is legal authorization for organ and tissue donation.
questions.why: For people 18 and over, being in the donor registry is legal permission for organ and tissue donation. (Driver's Manual, page 8)
wrong: The age is 18, not 21.
The age is 18, not 16.
There is an age limit. It is 18 and over.

questions.q: After you sign up as an organ and tissue donor at the DMV, what does the manual ask you to do?
options: Renew the choice every year by mail
Carry a separate donor card at all times
Notify your insurance company in writing
Tell your family about your decision
questions.ref: p.9 (continued from p.8): please be sure to inform your family of your decision to be an organ and tissue donor.
questions.why: Be sure to tell your family about your decision to be an organ and tissue donor. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: The manual does not require a yearly renewal. It asks you to tell your family.
The donor mark goes on your license. The manual asks you to tell your family.
The manual does not mention insurance. It asks you to tell your family.

questions.q: You apply for voter registration while renewing your license at the DMV. About how long until you should get a confirmation notice from your town's registrar of voters?
options: About six months
About 60 days
About three weeks
About one week
questions.ref: p.9 Registering to Vote: you should receive a confirmation notice in approximately three (3) weeks from the registrar of voters in your city or town.
questions.why: You should get a confirmation notice from your town's registrar of voters in about three weeks. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: The manual says about three weeks, not six months.
The manual says about three weeks, not 60 days.
The manual says about three weeks, not one week.

questions.q: You move to a new town and file a change of address with the DMV, but you do NOT want it used for voting records. What should you do?
options: Nothing; the DMV never shares any change of address information
Ask the DMV to cancel your current voter registration
File the change of address only after the next election
Indicate on the form that it is not for voter registration
questions.ref: p.9 Registering to Vote: your change of address form will be used to update your voter registration record unless you indicate on the form that it is NOT for voter registration purposes.
questions.why: Your DMV change of address updates your voter record unless you mark on the form that it is not for voter registration. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: The DMV does use your change of address to update voter records, unless you say no on the form.
You do not need to cancel. Just mark the form as not for voter registration.
Waiting is not the manual's advice. Mark the form as not for voter registration.

questions.q: Which statement about registering to vote through the DMV is correct?
options: You may apply only when you first get a license
You may apply or update your registration at any time
You may apply only in the month before an election
You may apply only at your town's registrar office
questions.ref: p.9 Registering to Vote: you can apply for voter registration or update your information through DMV at any time; you are offered the chance when you apply for, renew or replace a license or ID.
questions.why: You can apply for voter registration or update it through the DMV at any time. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: You are offered the chance at license visits, but you may apply at any time.
There is no one-month window. You may apply at any time.
You may apply through the DMV, not only at the registrar.

questions.q: You choose to apply for voter registration at the DMV. What does the DMV do next?
options: Gives you a receipt and sends your application to election officials
Gives you a paper form to mail to the governor's office
Registers you itself and then mails your new voter card to you within 20 days
Adds a voter insignia to your license for a $30 fee
questions.ref: p.9 Registering to Vote: DMV will provide you with a receipt and will transmit your voter registration application information to election officials.
questions.why: The DMV gives you a receipt and sends your voter application to election officials. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: The DMV sends your application to election officials, not the governor.
The DMV passes your application on. Your town registrar sends a confirmation in about three weeks.
There is no voter mark on a license. Thirty dollars is the duplicate license fee.

questions.q: Who helped the Connecticut DMV develop the Limited Driver's License program?
options: The Office of the Secretary of State
The DMV Commissioner's Advisory Committee on Teen Safe Driving
The Bureau of Rehabilitation Services
Its Medical Advisory Board of volunteer doctors
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: the DMV, with the help of its Medical Advisory Board (medical doctors who volunteer their time), developed the Limited Driver's License program.
questions.why: The DMV built the Limited Driver's License program with help from its Medical Advisory Board, a group of volunteer doctors. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: The Secretary of State's office handles online voter sign-up, not limited licenses.
The teen safe driving committee works on teen driving, not limited licenses.
The Bureau of Rehabilitation Services runs disabled driver training, not this program.

questions.q: A driver's physical abilities have changed since she was first licensed. Before a limited license is issued, what may be required?
options: A second 8-hour safe driving course and the CS-1 form
Reports from one or more physicians and an on-road skills test
A signed statement from a licensed home driving instructor
A new 25-question knowledge test and a new photo learner's permit
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: reports made by one or more physicians must be submitted and the person may be required to pass an on-the-road skills test with a DMV inspector.
questions.why: Before a limited license is issued, reports from one or more doctors must be sent in. The person may also need an on-the-road skills test with a DMV inspector. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: The 8-hour course is for new drivers, not for limited licenses.
A home instructor statement is for home-trained teens, not limited licenses.
The manual asks for doctor reports and maybe a road test, not a new permit.

questions.q: A person with a medical condition that affects driving is moving to Connecticut. How far ahead of applying for a license does the manual recommend contacting the Driver Services Division?
options: At least one year
At least 30 days
At least four months
At least two weeks
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: contact the Driver Services Division at least four months prior to applying for a Connecticut license, whether a new driver or a new resident.
questions.why: Contact the Driver Services Division at least four months before applying for a Connecticut license. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: The manual says at least four months, not a year.
The manual says at least four months, not 30 days.
The manual says at least four months, not two weeks.

questions.q: Which statement about the Limited Licenses Program is FALSE?
options: It is for people whose physical abilities changed
Its restrictions are noted on the license document
It may require an on-road test with an inspector
It is only for drivers who were already licensed
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: it also allows DMV to issue new licenses to persons who previously would not have qualified; restrictions are noted on the license document.
questions.why: This is false. The program also lets DMV issue new licenses to people who would not have qualified before. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: This is true. The program is for people whose physical abilities have changed.
This is true. The restrictions are noted on the license.
This is true. An on-the-road skills test may be required.

questions.q: For which type of license holder are the health standards more stringent?
options: A bus or taxi driver carrying passengers
A driver renewing a Class D license
A 16-year-old with a new Class D license
A driver with a daylight-only license
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: health standards are more stringent for CDL holders or holders of a license to operate a vehicle carrying passengers (taxi, delivery vehicle, bus, school bus, etc.).
questions.why: Health standards are stricter for commercial license holders and for drivers who carry passengers, such as taxi and bus drivers. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: A regular Class D renewal is not named for stricter health standards.
A new Class D driver is not named for stricter health standards.
A daylight-only limit is a restriction, not a stricter health standard.

questions.q: A limited license may restrict a driver to using corrective lenses. Which kind of lenses does this restriction NOT include?
options: Bifocal eyeglasses
Prescription glasses
Telescopic lenses
Soft contact lenses
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: restriction when using corrective lenses (not including telescopic lenses) as prescribed by a licensed optometrist or ophthalmologist.
questions.why: The corrective lens restriction does not include telescopic lenses. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: Bifocals are corrective lenses. Only telescopic lenses are left out.
Prescription glasses are corrective lenses. Only telescopic lenses are left out.
Contact lenses are corrective lenses. Only telescopic lenses are left out.

questions.q: A driver's limited license says she may drive only on highways that are not limited access highways. Which road may she NOT use?
options: A two-lane country road with no exits
A limited access interstate highway
A local road that passes through a school zone
A city street in the town where she lives
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: one restriction permits operation only on highways that are not limited access highways.
questions.why: This restriction lets her drive only on highways that are not limited access. So a limited access interstate is off-limits. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: A country road is not a limited access highway, so she may use it.
A local road is not a limited access highway, so she may use it.
A city street is not a limited access highway, so she may use it.

questions.q: A limited license may require outside mirrors on both the left and right sides of the vehicle. How far to the rear must those mirrors show the driver a view of the highway?
options: At least 50 feet
At least 200 feet
At least 500 feet
At least 100 feet
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: external mirrors on both left and right sides to reflect a view of the highway at least 200 feet to the rear.
questions.why: The mirrors must show the driver a view of the highway at least 200 feet to the rear. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: The manual says at least 200 feet, not 50.
The manual says at least 200 feet, not 500.
The manual says at least 200 feet, not 100.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the restrictions a limited license may contain?
options: Driving only with a licensed passenger
Driving only an automatic-shift car
Driving only in the period of daylight
Driving only with special controls
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: listed restrictions are daylight, corrective lenses, non-limited-access highways, automatic transmission, left and right external mirrors, and special controls or equipment.
questions.why: The listed limits are daylight, lenses, no limited access highways, automatic transmission, mirrors, and special controls. A licensed passenger is not on the list. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: Driving only an automatic transmission car is on the list.
Driving only in daylight is on the list.
Driving only with special controls or equipment is on the list.

questions.q: Which statement about people with medical conditions or limitations is correct according to the manual?
options: They can drive only if they pass a new road test every single year
They may drive only if a licensed adult rides with them on every trip
They can never be licensed again once a condition appears after first licensing
They may still drive safely if the condition is stable and doctor-monitored
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: a person with certain conditions may still be able to drive safely if such conditions have been stabilized and are monitored by the person's physician.
questions.why: A person with certain conditions may still drive safely if the condition is stable and watched by their doctor. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: The manual does not require a yearly road test. A road test may be required before a limited license.
The manual does not require a licensed adult on every trip.
The limited license program is for people whose abilities changed after first licensing.

questions.q: A permanent Connecticut resident with a disability wants training to drive with special adaptive equipment. Which agency does the manual say to contact?
options: The DMV Medical Review Division
The Office of the Secretary of State
The state Bureau of Rehabilitation Services
A licensed Connecticut commercial driving school
questions.ref: p.9 Disabled Driver Training Services: residents interested in the program should contact the state Bureau of Rehabilitation Services.
questions.why: Residents who want training to drive with special equipment should contact the state Bureau of Rehabilitation Services. (Driver's Manual, page 9)
wrong: The manual names the Bureau of Rehabilitation Services for this training.
The Secretary of State handles voting, not driver training.
The manual names the Bureau of Rehabilitation Services for this training.

questions.q: The DMV's teen safe driving message in the manual says "You're NOT just along for the ride." Who does it say has a responsibility for safety?
options: Only the driver who holds the license
Only the driving school instructors
Only parents who set household rules
Everyone, including teen passengers
questions.ref: p.10 Teen safe driving page ("There are two ways to go"): Safety is EVERYONE's responsibility. Teen drivers and passengers like you have a responsibility for safety, too.
questions.why: The page says safety is everyone's responsibility. Teen drivers and passengers both have a responsibility for safety. (Driver's Manual, page 10)
wrong: The message says passengers have a responsibility too, not only the driver.
The message says safety is everyone's job, not only instructors.
The message says safety is everyone's job, not only parents.

questions.q: Which statement about a vehicle that is in bad shape is TRUE according to the manual?
options: It costs less to run since you skip the repairs
It is safe as long as it passed its last emissions test
It costs more to run than one that is maintained
It gives you an extra safety margin in an emergency
questions.ref: p.11 Know Your Vehicle Inside and Out: a vehicle in bad shape is unsafe and costs more to run than one that is maintained; a vehicle in good shape gives an extra safety margin.
questions.why: A vehicle in bad shape is unsafe and costs more to run than one that is kept up. (Driver's Manual, page 11)
wrong: It costs more to run, not less.
Passing emissions does not make a car in bad shape safe.
A car in good shape gives you the extra safety margin, not one in bad shape.

questions.q: While stopping at a light, your brake pedal sinks all the way to the floor. What does the manual say to do?
options: Replace the bulbs in the brake lights
Have the headlights realigned
Have a mechanic check the brakes
Add air to all four tires
questions.ref: p.11 Braking System: if the brakes make a lot of noise, emit an unusual odor, or the brake pedal goes to the floor, have a mechanic check them.
questions.why: If the brake pedal goes to the floor, have a mechanic check your brakes. (Driver's Manual, page 11)
wrong: Brake lights only warn others. A pedal that sinks means the brakes need a mechanic.
Headlights have nothing to do with a sinking brake pedal.
Tire air will not fix a brake pedal that goes to the floor.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed in the manual as a sign that your brakes should be checked by a mechanic?
options: The steering wheel is hard to turn when parked
The car pulls to one side when braking
The brakes give off an unusual odor
The brakes make a lot of noise when they are used
questions.ref: p.11 Braking System: have brakes checked if they make a lot of noise, emit an unusual odor, the pedal goes to the floor, or the vehicle pulls to one side when braking.
questions.why: Hard steering points to the steering system, not the brakes. Signs of brake trouble include noise, an odd smell, a sinking pedal, or pulling to one side. (Driver's Manual, pages 11 and 12)
wrong: Pulling to one side when braking is listed as a brake problem.
An unusual odor is listed as a brake problem.
A lot of noise is listed as a brake problem.

questions.q: How does the manual say you should check that your turn signals, brake lights, taillights, and headlights are working?
options: Only at night on the road
From the dashboard lights
From outside the vehicle
Only at an emissions station
questions.ref: p.11 Lights: make sure turn signals, brake lights, taillights, and headlights are operating properly; these should be checked from the outside of the vehicle.
questions.why: Check your turn signals, brake lights, taillights, and headlights from outside the vehicle. (Driver's Manual, page 11)
wrong: The manual says to check from outside the car, not only at night.
The manual says to check from outside, not from dashboard lights.
You can check them yourself from outside the car.

questions.q: Your windshield wiper blades leave streaks and are not clearing water well. What does the manual say to do?
options: Run them at full speed
Replace the blades
Only use them in snow
Use the defroster instead
questions.ref: p.11 Windshield, Wipers, Windows: if the blades are not clearing water well, replace them.
questions.why: If the wiper blades are not clearing water well, replace them. (Driver's Manual, page 11)
wrong: Running bad blades faster will not fix them. Replace them.
Wipers clear both rain and snow, so you need good blades all the time.
The defroster does not clear rain. Replace the blades.

questions.q: Why does the manual say to keep the inside of your windshield and windows clean?
options: Smudges on the inside can make the windshield glass crack in cold weather
Bright sun or headlights on a dirty windshield make it hard to see
A dirty windshield will make the car fail the emissions inspection
Dirt on the inside of the glass can make the defroster stop working
questions.ref: p.11 Windshield, Wipers, Windows: make sure the inside of the windshield and windows are clean; bright sun or headlights on a dirty windshield make it hard to see.
questions.why: Bright sun or headlights shining on a dirty windshield make it hard to see. (Driver's Manual, page 11)
wrong: The manual's reason is glare that makes it hard to see, not cracking.
The manual's reason is glare that makes it hard to see, not emissions.
The manual's reason is glare that makes it hard to see, not the defroster.

questions.q: Your windshield has a crack from a stone chip. What does the manual recommend?
options: Replace it only if the crack grows larger
Leave it alone unless it blocks your view
Cover the crack with clear tape to seal it
Have the damaged windshield replaced
questions.ref: p.11 Windshield, Wipers, Windows: damaged glass can break very easily in a minor collision or when something hits the windshield; have a damaged windshield replaced.
questions.why: Damaged glass can break very easily in a minor crash or when something hits it. Have a damaged windshield replaced. (Driver's Manual, page 11)
wrong: Do not wait. Damaged glass can break easily, so replace it.
Even if you can see, damaged glass can break easily in a minor crash.
Tape does not make the glass strong. Replace the windshield.

questions.q: Which statement about windshield wipers is TRUE according to the manual?
options: Wipers are needed for rain only, so they don't matter in snow
Some vehicles also have wipers for the rear window and headlights
Wiper blades only need to be replaced when the windshield is replaced
The window washer bottle should be kept only half full in winter
questions.ref: p.11 Windshield, Wipers, Windows: wipers keep rain and snow off the windshield; some vehicles have wipers for rear windows and headlights; keep your window washer bottle full.
questions.why: Some vehicles also have wipers for the rear window and headlights. Make sure all wipers work well. (Driver's Manual, page 11)
wrong: Wipers keep both rain and snow off the windshield.
Replace blades whenever they stop clearing water well.
The manual says to keep your washer bottle full.

questions.q: You are driving on a wet road with worn, bald tires. According to the manual, what effect do the tires have?
options: No effect unless the tire pressure is also low
Better grip because more rubber touches the road
Longer stopping distance and harder turning
Lower risk of hydroplaning on standing water
questions.ref: p.11 Tires: worn or bald tires can increase your stopping distance and make turning more difficult when the road is wet; worn tires increase hydroplaning.
questions.why: Worn or bald tires can make your stopping distance longer and make turning harder on a wet road. (Driver's Manual, page 11)
wrong: Worn tires cause these problems even with the right air pressure.
Worn tires grip worse, not better.
Worn tires make hydroplaning worse, not better.

questions.q: Which statement about worn tires is FALSE according to the manual?
options: They lower the chance of a flat tire
They make turning harder on wet roads
They can increase your stopping distance
They increase the effect of hydroplaning
questions.ref: p.11 Tires: worn tires increase the effect of hydroplaning and increase the chance of having a flat tire; worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder when wet.
questions.why: This is false. Worn tires raise the chance of a flat tire. (Driver's Manual, page 11)
wrong: This is true. Worn tires make turning harder on wet roads.
This is true. Worn tires can make your stopping distance longer.
This is true. Worn tires make hydroplaning worse.

questions.q: While driving, your car bounces and the steering wheel shakes. What does the manual say to do?
options: Speed up slightly to smooth out the ride
Use only the parking brake to slow down
Have a mechanic check it
Let some air out of all four tires
questions.ref: p.11 Tires: if the vehicle bounces, the steering wheel shakes, or the vehicle pulls to one side, have a mechanic check it.
questions.why: If your car bounces, the steering wheel shakes, or it pulls to one side, have a mechanic check it. (Driver's Manual, page 11)
wrong: Speeding up is not the fix. Have a mechanic check it.
The manual's advice is to see a mechanic, not to brake differently.
Low tire pressure makes the car harder to steer and stop.

questions.q: How often does the manual say you should check your tires for wear and damage?
options: Only when a tire warning light comes on
Once every month, or before a long trip
Every time you fill up the gas tank
Once a year, at the emissions test
questions.ref: p.11 Tires: once every month, or before you embark upon a long road trip, check your tires for wear and damage problems.
questions.why: Check your tires for wear and damage once a month, or before a long road trip. (Driver's Manual, page 11)
wrong: Do not wait for a light. Check once a month or before a long trip.
The manual says once a month or before a long trip, not at every fill-up.
Once a year is not enough. Check once a month.

questions.q: You are about to do the penny test on your tire. Where on the tire should you place the penny?
options: At a point where the tread appears to be highest
On the tire sidewall next to the psi rating
At a point where the tread appears to be lowest
Between the tire and the edge of the wheel rim
questions.ref: p.11 Tires (penny test): select a point on your tire where the tread appears to be lowest and place Lincoln's head into one of the grooves.
questions.why: Put the penny in a groove where the tread looks lowest. If part of Lincoln's head is covered, you have enough tread. (Driver's Manual, page 11)
wrong: Test where the tread looks lowest, not highest.
The penny goes into a tread groove, not on the sidewall.
The penny goes into a tread groove, not by the rim.

questions.q: You turn off a paved road onto a long dirt road. According to the manual, how does this change your driving?
options: You have less traction, so stopping takes longer and skids are easier when turning
Traction improves because loose dirt helps the tires grip, so you can keep your speed
Traction is lower, but only when braking; turning on dirt is no harder than on asphalt
Traction is the same as asphalt as long as your tires have the correct air pressure
questions.ref: p.25 Tire Conditions: there is less traction on gravel or dirt than on concrete or asphalt; you must slow down, stopping takes much longer and it is easier to skid when turning.
questions.why: You have less traction on gravel or dirt than on pavement. You must slow down, stopping takes much longer, and it is easier to skid when turning. (Driver's Manual, page 25)
wrong: Dirt gives you less traction, not more, so you must slow down.
The manual says it is also easier to skid when turning on dirt.
Dirt has less traction than pavement no matter what your tire pressure is.

questions.q: Bald or badly worn tires are on your car and it starts to rain. Compared with good tires, when will they begin to lose traction on the wet road?
options: At much lower speeds than about 35 mph
Only above 55 mph, when hydroplaning begins for all tires
Only in heavy rain; in light rain worn tires grip like new ones
At about 35 mph, the same speed as tires in good condition
questions.ref: p.25 Water on the Roadway: most tires have good traction up to about 35 mph on wet roads; bald or badly worn tires lose traction at much lower speeds.
questions.why: Most tires grip well on wet roads up to about 35 miles per hour. Bald or badly worn tires lose traction at much lower speeds. (Driver's Manual, page 25)
wrong: Hydroplaning can start above about 35 miles per hour, and worn tires lose grip even sooner.
Worn tires do not grip like new ones. They lose traction at much lower speeds.
Worn tires lose traction at much lower speeds than good tires.

questions.q: While driving in the rain, it feels like your tires have lost traction. You must make a turn to avoid a hazard. According to the manual, how should you turn?
options: Sharply, while pressing the brake pedal firmly
Quickly, so you spend less time on the water
After speeding up slightly so the tires bite into the road
Slowly, or you will cause the vehicle to skid
questions.ref: p.25 Water on the Roadway: keep the wheel straight; only turn in an emergency, and if you must turn, do it slowly or you will cause the vehicle to skid.
questions.why: Keep the wheel straight and turn only in an emergency. If you must turn, do it slowly, or you will cause a skid. (Driver's Manual, page 25)
wrong: Do not try to stop or turn hard until your tires are gripping the road again.
Turning quickly can make the car skid. Turn slowly.
Ease off the gas, do not speed up.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the reasons the manual gives for the increase in aggressive driving incidents?
options: Higher posted speed limits on interstate highways
Increased traffic congestion on roads
A general decline in courtesy and civility
Youths who drive but lack the maturity to handle tense situations
questions.ref: p.25-26 Reasons for Aggressive Driving: congestion, parents modeling aggression, decline in courtesy, immature youth drivers, outside conflicts, sense of territory, false sense of safety; speed limits are not listed.
questions.why: The manual lists congestion, less courtesy, immature young drivers, and outside stress as reasons. Higher speed limits are not on the list. (Driver's Manual, pages 25 and 26)
wrong: Increased traffic congestion is on the list.
A general decline in courtesy is on the list.
Young drivers who lack maturity are on the list.

questions.q: A driver believes he owns the space around his car and wants to strike back whenever another vehicle 'invades' it. Which cause of aggressive driving does the manual say this is?
options: A false sense of immunity in safer vehicles
Conflicts from family or job issues
Increased traffic congestion
A sense of territory
questions.ref: p.26 Reasons for Aggressive Driving: a sense of 'territory' leads people to presume they own the space around their vehicles and to strike back when it is invaded.
questions.why: A sense of territory makes people think they own the space around their car. They then want to strike back when someone enters it. (Driver's Manual, page 26)
wrong: That cause is about feeling safe in a car, not about owning space.
That cause is about stress from home or work, not owning space.
That cause is about crowded roads, not owning space.

questions.q: Another driver cuts you off aggressively and keeps driving dangerously. According to the manual, what is the best way to handle it?
options: Follow closely so you can read the license plate to report it
Flash your high beams so the driver knows it was noticed
Pull alongside at the next light and explain the danger calmly
Leave punishment to police; report it when you arrive
questions.ref: p.26 How to Avoid Conflict on the Road: leave punishment to the police; call the police to report aggressive driving when you arrive at your destination.
questions.why: Leave punishment to the police. Call to report aggressive driving when you get where you are going. (Driver's Manual, page 26)
wrong: Following closely is tailgating, which can start fights.
Do not use your lights to retaliate against other drivers.
Do not engage with an aggressive driver. Get out of the way.

questions.q: A driver in the next lane keeps speeding up whenever you do, as if trying to race you. What does the manual advise?
options: Don't compete; let the driver who is racing pass you
Hold your speed so the other driver cannot get ahead
Speed up briefly to get clear of the other driver
Sound your horn to warn the driver to stop racing
questions.ref: p.26 How to Avoid Conflict on the Road: don't compete on the road; driving is not a contest; let others who are racing pass you.
questions.why: Don't compete on the road. Driving is not a contest, so let anyone who is racing pass you. (Driver's Manual, page 26)
wrong: Holding your speed turns it into a contest. Let them pass.
Speeding up is competing. Let the other driver go by.
Honking can set off a stressed driver. Just let them pass.

questions.q: According to the manual, how should you think about another driver who has just done something aggressive to you?
options: Assume it was on purpose and stay right behind to watch the driver
Assume the driver is impaired and follow until police arrive
Give the benefit of the doubt; it was likely a mistake
Assume the driver wants to race and move out of the way fast
questions.ref: p.26 How to Avoid Conflict on the Road: give an aggressive driver the benefit of the doubt; he or she likely made a mistake from fatigue or inattention, not intentionally.
questions.why: Give an aggressive driver the benefit of the doubt. They likely made a mistake from being tired or not paying attention. (Driver's Manual, page 26)
wrong: The manual says to give the benefit of the doubt, not assume it was on purpose.
The manual says to leave it to police, not to follow the driver.
The manual says it was likely a mistake, not a challenge to race.

questions.q: You are cruising on a multi-lane highway in the far left lane and a faster car comes up behind you. What does the manual say about lane blocking?
options: Stay in the left lane at the limit; the other driver must wait
Yield to the right and let the faster car pass
Speed up to match the flow so you can stay in the passing lane
Tap your brakes so the driver backs off before you move over
questions.ref: p.26 Behaviors That Can Cause Trouble, Lane Blocking: don't block the passing lane; stay out of the far left lane and yield to the right for any vehicle that wants to pass.
questions.why: Don't block the passing lane. Stay out of the far left lane and move right for anyone who wants to pass. (Driver's Manual, page 26)
wrong: Blocking the passing lane is a behavior that can cause trouble.
Stay out of the far left lane unless passing, instead of speeding up to hold it.
Never slow down quickly to discourage a driver behind you. It raises your risk of being hit.

questions.q: In a non-emergency, you need to get another driver's attention. How does the manual say you should use your horn?
options: Give one long, firm blast
Tap it lightly
Hold it until the driver responds
Honk twice quickly
questions.ref: p.26 Behaviors That Can Cause Trouble, Horn: use your horn sparingly; in a non-emergency, tap your horn lightly.
questions.why: Use your horn sparingly. In a non-emergency, tap it lightly. (Driver's Manual, page 26)
wrong: A sharp blast is only for real danger.
Use the horn sparingly. Holding it down can set off a stressed driver.
The manual says to tap it lightly, not honk twice.

questions.q: You are not planning to turn right at the next few intersections. According to the manual's list of behaviors that can cause trouble, what should you do?
options: Avoid the right-hand lane
Stay in the right-hand lane and let drivers go around you
Use the far left lane until you need to turn
Use the right lane, since it is the slowest lane
questions.ref: p.26 Behaviors That Can Cause Trouble, Failure to Turn: right turns are allowed after a stop at a red light in most areas; avoid the right-hand lane if you are not turning right.
questions.why: Right turns on red are allowed in most areas. So avoid the right-hand lane if you are not turning right. (Driver's Manual, page 26)
wrong: Blocking the right lane holds up drivers who want to turn right on red.
The manual also says stay out of the far left lane except to pass.
The manual says to avoid the right lane if you are not turning right.

questions.q: At night an oncoming driver does not dim his high beams. Which response does the manual warn you NOT to use?
options: Flash your headlights quickly a couple of times
Look toward the right side of the road
Keep your own headlights on low beam
Switch on your high beams to 'teach a lesson'
questions.ref: p.26 Behaviors That Can Cause Trouble, Headlights: don't retaliate to oncoming high beams with your own to 'teach them a lesson'; p.38 Lights: if an oncoming driver keeps high beams on, flash your headlights quickly a couple of times, then look toward the right side of the road; do not try to 'get back' with your bright lights.
questions.why: Don't answer oncoming high beams with your own to teach them a lesson. You may both be blinded. (Driver's Manual, pages 26 and 38)
wrong: The manual says this is the right first step.
The manual says to look to the right side of the road so you are not blinded.
The manual says to keep your lights on low beam and dim them for oncoming traffic.

questions.q: Which rule does the manual tell you to use at night to make sure you are not over-driving your headlights?
options: The two-second following-distance rule
The 12-second visual lead time rule
The four-second sight-distance rule
The three-to-four-second space rule
questions.ref: p.26 Behaviors That Can Cause Trouble, Headlights: use the 'four-second sight-distance rule' at night to make sure you are not over-driving your headlights.
questions.why: Use the four-second sight-distance rule at night to make sure you are not over-driving your headlights. (Driver's Manual, page 26)
wrong: The manual names the four-second sight-distance rule, not a two-second rule.
The 12-second rule is about looking well ahead, not night headlight range.
The 3 to 4 second space is for following certain vehicles, not checking headlight range.

questions.q: You are driving in the right-hand lane of a multi-lane highway as you approach an on-ramp with cars trying to merge. What does the manual suggest?
options: Stay in your lane; merging cars must stop and wait for a gap
Speed up so the merging cars can fit in behind you
When traffic permits, move out of the right lane
Slow nearly to a stop on the highway to let them enter
questions.ref: p.26 Behaviors That Can Cause Trouble, Merging: when traffic permits, move out of the right-hand lane of a multi-lane highway to allow vehicles to enter from the on-ramps.
questions.why: When traffic allows, move out of the right lane of a multi-lane highway. This lets cars enter from the on-ramps. (Driver's Manual, page 26)
wrong: The manual asks you to make room for merging cars when you can.
Speeding up is not the manual's advice. Move over a lane if traffic allows.
Slowing nearly to a stop on the highway could cause a rear-end crash.

questions.q: You are towing a trailer and a long line of cars has built up behind you. What does the manual say to do?
options: Speed up past the limit so you stop holding up traffic
Turn on your hazard lights and keep going at the same speed
Pull over when you can so the cars behind can pass
Keep going; drivers must wait behind a vehicle towing a trailer
questions.ref: p.26 Behaviors That Can Cause Trouble, Blocking Traffic: if pulling a trailer or driving a cumbersome vehicle that impedes traffic, pull over when you have the opportunity so motorists can pass.
questions.why: If you are pulling a trailer and holding up traffic, pull over when you can so the drivers behind can pass. (Driver's Manual, page 26)
wrong: Never speed past the limit. Pull over to let them pass.
Hazard lights are for car trouble. Pull over to let traffic pass.
The manual says to pull over when you can so others can pass.

questions.q: You are shopping for an anti-theft car alarm. What kind does the manual recommend?
options: One that sounds until the owner returns to the car
One that also flashes the headlights on high beam
One that sounds whenever the car is bumped
One that turns off after a short time
questions.ref: p.26 Behaviors That Can Cause Trouble, Alarms: learn to turn your alarm off quickly; when buying an alarm, select one that turns off after a short period of time.
questions.why: When buying an alarm, choose one that turns off after a short time. (Driver's Manual, page 26)
wrong: The manual says to pick one that turns off after a short time.
The manual says to pick one that turns off after a short time.
The manual says to pick one that turns off after a short time.

questions.q: A hostile motorist pulls alongside you at a light and is trying to pick a fight. What does the manual advise?
options: Make brief eye contact and nod so the driver sees you're no threat
Roll down your window and calmly apologize to calm things down
Avoid eye contact and get out of the way
Look the driver in the eye to show you will not be intimidated
questions.ref: p.26 Behaviors That Can Cause Trouble, Eye Contact: do not make eye contact, which can be seen as a challenge; get out of the way and do not acknowledge the other driver.
questions.why: Do not make eye contact with a hostile driver. It can be seen as a challenge. Get out of the way and do not respond. (Driver's Manual, page 26)
wrong: Any eye contact can be seen as a challenge, so avoid it.
Do not acknowledge the other driver at all.
Looking them in the eye can push them toward violence.

questions.q: Which of these does the manual list as a behavior that has resulted in violence from angry motorists?
options: Blocking the road to talk to a pedestrian
Driving in the right lane on a multi-lane highway
Waving to another driver using all of your fingers
Keeping your headlights on low beam on a lit city street
questions.ref: p.26 Behaviors That Can Cause Trouble, Blocking Traffic: do not block the road while talking to a pedestrian on the sidewalk; this behavior has resulted in violence.
questions.why: Blocking the road while talking to a pedestrian on the sidewalk has led to violence from angry drivers. (Driver's Manual, page 26)
wrong: The manual does not list right-lane driving as causing violence.
The manual says to wave using all of your fingers. Obscene gestures cause trouble.
The manual says to keep your lights on low beam unless it is dark and unlit.

questions.q: Which of these does the manual list as a possible distraction OUTSIDE a moving vehicle?
options: Attending to children or pets in the car
Reading billboards along the road
Grooming, such as shaving or combing hair
Picking up something that fell on the floor
questions.ref: p.27 Driver Distractions: outside distractions include outside traffic, police pulling someone over, sunlight, crash scenes, road construction and reading billboards; the others are inside distractions.
questions.why: Reading billboards and road ads is listed as a distraction outside the vehicle. (Driver's Manual, page 27)
wrong: Caring for kids or pets is listed as an inside distraction.
Grooming is listed as an inside distraction.
Picking up something that fell is listed as an inside distraction.

questions.q: Your eyes are on the road, but your mind is on a big argument you had at school. How does the manual rate this kind of distraction?
options: Safe, as long as both hands stay on the steering wheel
Less dangerous, because your eyes are still on the road
Just as dangerous as eyes-off-road distractions
A problem only if you are also talking on a phone
questions.ref: p.27 Driver Distractions: mental activities that take your mind away from driving are just as dangerous; your eyes can gaze at objects but fail to see them.
questions.why: Mental activities that take your mind off driving are just as dangerous as looking away. Your eyes can look at things but fail to see them. (Driver's Manual, page 27)
wrong: Having both hands on the wheel does not help if your mind is somewhere else.
Your eyes can be on the road and still miss things when your mind is elsewhere.
Mental distraction is dangerous by itself, even without a phone.

questions.q: You are taking your dog to the vet. What does the manual say to do before moving your vehicle?
options: Let it sit in the front seat so you can watch it
Hold its leash in one hand while you steer with the other
Secure it in a pet carrier or portable kennel
Open a window so the pet stays calm during the trip
questions.ref: p.27 Driver Distractions: properly secure pets in a pet carrier or portable kennel before moving your vehicle.
questions.why: Secure pets in a pet carrier or portable kennel before you start driving. (Driver's Manual, page 27)
wrong: A loose pet is a distraction. Put it in a carrier or kennel.
Holding a leash takes a hand off the wheel. Use a carrier.
The manual says to secure the pet in a carrier, not open a window.

questions.q: You are driving to an unfamiliar town and need to check the map partway there. What does the manual say?
options: Stop in a safe parking area to look at the map
Hold it at eye level so the road stays in view
Look at it while slowly driving on the shoulder
Glance at it only while traveling below 25 mph
questions.ref: p.27 Driver Distractions: review maps and plan your route before driving; if you need to look at a map while driving, stop in a safe parking area.
questions.why: Plan your route before you go. If you need to check a map while driving, stop in a safe parking area. (Driver's Manual, page 27)
wrong: Do not read a map while driving at all. Stop first.
Never drive on the shoulder. Stop in a safe parking area.
There is no safe speed for reading a map. Stop first.

questions.q: Which of these does the manual say can be deadly when combined with driving?
options: Adjusting your mirrors before the trip
Planning your route before you leave
Wearing headphones to listen to music
Adjusting controls at a normal stop
questions.ref: p.27 Driver Distractions: do not talk with friends in other vehicles or wear headphones to listen to music; these can be deadly when combined with driving.
questions.why: Wearing headphones to listen to music, or talking with friends in other cars, can be deadly when combined with driving. (Driver's Manual, page 27)
wrong: Adjusting mirrors before you drive is a good habit.
Planning your route before you leave is advice the manual gives.
Using normal stops to adjust controls is advice the manual gives.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the manual's signs that another driver may be distracted?
options: A vehicle traveling at inconsistent speeds
A vehicle that has an out-of-state license plate
A driver who appears to be arguing with passengers
A driver of a slow-moving or commercial vehicle
questions.ref: p.27 Driver Distractions: watch for drifting vehicles, inconsistent speeds, drivers busy with objects, drivers arguing with passengers, and drivers of slow-moving or commercial vehicles.
questions.why: The manual lists signs of a distracted driver, like drifting, uneven speeds, drivers busy with objects, drivers arguing with passengers, and drivers of slow-moving or commercial vehicles. Where a car is registered is not on that list. (Driver's Manual, p. 27)
wrong: Inconsistent speed is on the manual's list of signs of a distracted driver.
Drivers who seem to be arguing with passengers are on the manual's list.
Drivers of slow-moving or commercial vehicles are on the manual's list.

questions.q: You are distracted by a ringing phone and rear-end the car in front of you. According to the manual, who is responsible for the crash?
options: You are, not the distraction
The other driver, for stopping in front of you
No one, because the crash was an unavoidable accident
The caller, because the call caused the distraction
questions.ref: p.27 Driver Distractions: you are completely and solely responsible for operating your vehicle safely; if you are distracted and crash, the responsibility falls on you, not the distraction.
questions.why: You are completely and solely responsible for driving safely. If you are distracted and crash, the responsibility falls on you, not the distraction. (Driver's Manual, p. 27)
wrong: The manual puts the responsibility on you, the distracted driver.
The manual says the responsibility falls on you, so it is not a no-fault accident.
The manual says the responsibility falls on you, not on the distraction.

questions.q: According to the manual, which age group often needs more sleep than an average adult and is at special risk of a fatigue-related crash?
options: People 16 to 20 years old
People 21 to 30 years old
People 18 to 25 years old
People 16 to 24 years old
questions.ref: p.28 Fatigue: Young Adults - people 16 to 24 years old often need more sleep than an average adult.
questions.why: The manual says young adults from 16 to 24 years old often need more sleep than an average adult. That puts them at special risk for a fatigue-related crash. (Driver's Manual, p. 28)
wrong: The range is 16 to 24, so it goes past age 20.
The manual names 16 to 24, not 21 to 30.
The range starts at 16 and ends at 24.

questions.q: Your older brother just started working the night shift. According to the study the manual cites, about how much does night-shift work increase the risk of falling asleep at the wheel?
options: About 2 times
Nearly 6 times
Nearly 7 times
About 10 times
