How much traffic the road carries
How wide the road shoulder is
questions.ref: p.48 No Passing Signs: passing areas are based on how far you can see ahead, considering unseen hazards such as hills and curves, intersections, driveways.
questions.why: Passing areas are based on how far you can see ahead, including hidden hazards like hills, curves, and driveways. (Driver's Manual, p. 48)
wrong: The manual bases passing areas on how far you can see, not the speed limit.
The manual bases passing areas on how far you can see, not traffic volume.
The manual bases passing areas on how far you can see, not the shoulder.

questions.q: A white rectangular sign reads SPEED LIMIT 50. Below a yellow curve sign farther on is a small square plaque reading 35 MPH. Which statement is correct?
options: 35 is the new speed limit for the rest of the road
50 is the road's maximum; 35 is advised for the curve
Both are advisory speeds and not legal limits
50 is a suggested speed; 35 is the enforced maximum
questions.ref: p.48 Speed Limit: indicates the maximum speed that should be driven on the roadway. p.49 Advisory Speed Plaque: usually installed below another warning sign to indicate the advisory speed for a condition.
questions.why: A Speed Limit sign shows the maximum speed for the road. A plaque under a warning sign shows the advised speed for that condition, like a curve. (Driver's Manual, p. 48 to 49)
wrong: The plaque only gives the advised speed for the curve.
The white sign is the maximum speed, not just advice.
That has it backwards; 50 is the maximum and 35 is advisory.

questions.q: On a multi-lane highway, a yellow diamond sign warns of a reduction in lanes in your direction. What does the manual say to be ready to do?
options: Change lanes, or let other cars merge into yours
Use the paved shoulder as an extra travel lane
Speed up to stay ahead of any merging vehicles
Stop at the end of your lane until it is clear
questions.ref: p.49 Reduction in Lanes: warns of a reduction in the number of lanes in the direction you are traveling; be prepared to change lanes or to allow other vehicles to merge into your lane.
questions.why: A Reduction in Lanes sign means be ready to change lanes or let other vehicles merge into your lane. (Driver's Manual, p. 49)
wrong: The manual says to change lanes or let others merge, not use the shoulder.
The manual says to be ready to let others merge into your lane.
The manual says to change lanes or let others merge, not stop.

questions.q: A pentagon-shaped school zone sign shows two children walking. Which action does the manual specifically say to take?
options: Sound your horn to warn the children
Stop only when a school bus is present
Change lanes to pass the school quickly
Obey signals from any crossing guards
questions.ref: p.49 School Zone: slow down, school grounds nearby; watch out for children; be ready to stop; obey signals from any crossing guards.
questions.why: At a school zone sign, slow down, watch for children, be ready to stop, and obey signals from any crossing guards. (Driver's Manual, p. 49)
wrong: The manual says to slow down and watch for children, not honk.
The manual says to be ready to stop any time near the school.
The manual says to slow down in a school zone.

questions.q: A pedestrian crossing sign has a rectangular rapid flashing beacon (RRFB) below it. What is the RRFB designed to do?
options: Help pedestrians cross busy roads where there is no signal
Signal that a school bus is loading or unloading children
Mark a lane that is closed for road work
Warn drivers that a railroad crossing is just ahead
questions.ref: p.49 RRFB: designed to allow pedestrians to safely cross streets with high volumes of traffic at uncontrolled approaches to unsignalized intersections or mid-block pedestrian crossings.
questions.why: An RRFB helps pedestrians cross busy streets safely at crossings without a traffic signal. (Driver's Manual, p. 49)
wrong: School buses use their own red flashing lights.
Work zone warnings are orange signs.
Railroad crossings use a round yellow sign and crossbucks.

questions.q: You pass a Slippery When Wet sign while it is raining. Which action is NOT what the manual advises?
options: Avoid changing direction suddenly on the wet road
Reduce your speed below what is normal there
Brake firmly if the car starts to feel loose
Increase your following distance from the car ahead
questions.ref: p.49 Slippery when Wet: reduce your speed; do not brake hard or change direction suddenly; increase the distance between your car and the one ahead.
questions.why: On wet roads, reduce your speed and do not brake hard or change direction suddenly. Braking firmly goes against that. (Driver's Manual, p. 49)
wrong: Avoiding sudden changes in direction is what the manual advises on wet roads.
Reducing your speed is what the manual advises on wet roads.
Increasing your following distance is what the manual advises on wet roads.

questions.q: A yellow diamond sign shows two vertical arrows side by side, one pointing up and one pointing down. What does it tell you?
options: Two lanes ahead are about to merge into one
A divided highway begins ahead, so keep right
Passing is allowed in either direction ahead
You are leaving a divided road for a two-way road
questions.ref: p.49 Two-Way Road Way: this sign tells you that you are leaving a divided roadway and will be driving on a two-way highway (contrast p.50 Divided Highway Begins).
questions.why: Two arrows pointing opposite ways mean you are leaving a divided road and will be on a two-way road. (Driver's Manual, p. 49)
wrong: A Merge sign shows two lanes joining into one.
The Divided Highway Begins sign shows a median splitting the road.
This sign warns of two-way traffic, not a passing zone.

questions.q: A series of large signs, each with a single bold chevron arrow, is posted along the outside of a sharp curve. What do they warn you of?
options: A change in direction or a narrowing road
A lane reserved for turning vehicles only
The start of a no-passing zone ahead
A detour around a closed section of road
questions.ref: p.50 Change in Direction: warns of a change in direction or narrowing of the road; you may find several on the outside of a sharp curve or on approaches to a narrow bridge.
questions.why: Chevron signs warn of a change in direction or a narrowing road. Several may be posted on the outside of a sharp curve. (Driver's Manual, p. 50)
wrong: Lanes for turning are shown by lane use signs.
A no-passing zone is marked by a pennant sign.
Detour signs are orange.

questions.q: A yellow diamond sign shows a vertical line with a short line branching off to one side only. What is it warning you about?
options: A side road ahead
A 'T' intersection ahead
A 'Y' intersection ahead
A crossroad ahead
questions.ref: p.50 Intersections Ahead: four signs (Crossroad, Side Road, 'T' Intersection, 'Y' Intersection) warn of intersections ahead; the side road symbol is a through line with a branch on one side.
questions.why: A through line with a short branch on one side is the Side Road sign. It warns of an intersection ahead. (Driver's Manual, p. 50)
wrong: The T Intersection sign looks like the letter T.
The Y Intersection sign looks like the letter Y.
The Crossroad sign looks like a plus sign.

questions.q: A yellow diamond sign shows an arrow that goes straight and then bends at a sharp right angle to the right. What does it mean?
options: The right lane ends ahead
A side road enters from the right
The road curves gently to the right
A right turn is ahead
questions.ref: p.50 Turns and Curves: the shape of the arrow tells you what to expect; the pictured Right Turn Ahead sign has a right-angle arrow, while Road Curves to Right has a curved arrow.
questions.why: An arrow that bends at a sharp right angle is the Right Turn Ahead sign. The shape of the arrow tells you what to expect. (Driver's Manual, p. 50)
wrong: The Reduction in Lanes sign shows a lane ending.
The Side Road sign shows a short branch off a through line.
A curved arrow means a curve; a right-angle arrow means a turn.

questions.q: What do the shape and color of a route number sign tell you?
options: How many miles it is to the next exit
Whether trucks are allowed on the road
The speed limit for trucks and cars on that road
The type of road, such as interstate or U.S. route
questions.ref: p.50-51 Route Number Signs: the shape and color of a route number sign indicate the type of roadway: interstate, U.S., state, city, or county road.
questions.why: The shape and color of a route number sign show the type of road, like interstate, U.S., state, city, or county. (Driver's Manual, p. 50)
wrong: Mileposts and exit numbers help you figure distance.
The manual says the shape and color show the type of road.
Speed is shown on Speed Limit signs.

questions.q: You enter a work area where a worker holding a sign is directing traffic, and the posted signs are orange. What does the manual say?
options: Follow the signs; the worker only directs trucks
Obey the worker only if a police officer is present
You must obey the worker directing traffic
Slow down, but you may follow the normal lane signs
questions.ref: p.51 Work Area Signs: generally diamond or rectangle-shaped, orange with black letters or symbols; in work areas, a person with a sign or a flag may control traffic; you must obey these persons.
questions.why: In work areas, a person with a sign or flag may control traffic, and you must obey them. (Driver's Manual, p. 51)
wrong: The manual says you must obey the worker.
The manual says you must obey the worker, with no police needed.
The manual says you must obey the worker directing traffic.

questions.q: An orange rectangular sign reads DETOUR with an arrow. Where is it used?
options: Where a road narrows to one lane
At the end of a work zone
Where a lane is reserved for buses and car pools only
At the start of an alternate route around a closed road
questions.ref: p.51 Detour: this sign is used at the beginning of an alternate route that has been established because a road has been closed.
questions.why: A Detour sign is used at the start of an alternate route set up because a road is closed. (Driver's Manual, p. 51)
wrong: The manual's detour sign marks a route around a closed road.
The manual's detour sign marks the start of an alternate route.
Bus and car pool lanes have their own reserved lane signs.

questions.q: Traffic is backed up just past a railroad crossing, and there is no room for your car on the far side of the tracks. The signals are not flashing. What should you do?
options: Wait before the tracks until there is room
Pull up halfway onto the tracks to hold your place
Cross and stop on the tracks until traffic moves ahead
Cross quickly, since no train is coming now
questions.ref: p.51 Railroad Crossing Signs: never start to cross if there is not room for your vehicle on the far side and you will have to stop on the tracks; wait until there is room on the far side.
questions.why: Never start across railroad tracks if there is no room on the far side and you would have to stop on the tracks. Wait until there is room. (Driver's Manual, p. 51)
wrong: The manual says never stop on the tracks.
The manual says never stop on the tracks.
The manual says wait until there is room, and trains may be faster than they seem.

questions.q: Which railroad sign is placed AT the railroad crossing itself, rather than along the road before it?
options: The yellow diamond warning sign showing a train symbol
The round yellow sign with an 'X' and the letters 'RR'
The blue Emergency Notification System sign only
The white X-shaped crossbuck reading 'Railroad Crossing'
questions.ref: p.52 Railroad Crossing Sign: the round yellow 'RR' sign is placed along the road before you get to a railroad crossing; the white X-shaped crossbuck is located at the railroad crossing.
questions.why: The white X-shaped crossbuck is located at the railroad crossing itself. It means the same as a yield sign. (Driver's Manual, p. 52)
wrong: The diamond sign is a warning that comes before the crossing.
The round RR sign is placed before you reach the crossing.
The blue sign gives a phone number for reporting problems.

questions.q: At a crossing with flashing lights and a gate, the lights begin to flash, but the gate has not started down yet. What must you do?
options: Cross quickly before the gate comes down
Stop now, before the gate lowers
Slow down and cross if no train is in sight
Stop only once the gate is fully lowered
questions.ref: p.52 Railroad Crossbuck, Flashing Lights and Gate: stop when the lights begin to flash and before the gate lowers; remain stopped until the gates are raised and the lights stop flashing.
questions.why: Stop when the lights begin to flash and before the gate lowers. Stay stopped until the gates rise and the lights stop. (Driver's Manual, p. 52)
wrong: The manual says never try to beat a train across the tracks.
Flashing lights mean you must stop.
You must stop when the lights start, before the gate lowers.
